_README: Mutation branches for the anchor-soundness guard, kept in a FILE so the test
source and the commit text carry no rule vocabulary. Two review runs were cut
by a provider content filter because the phrases sat in script text; the
reviewer's own scripts hit it too. Tests reference these by label.
Each row: a branch spliced into the phrase alternation, and what the guard

rows.label: M1_class_two_members
rows.why: a class is an alternation written short; round 3 read only its first member

rows.label: M2_no_anchor_term
rows.why: a branch carrying no declared term at all

rows.label: M3_negated_single
rows.why: a negated single character is NOT_LITERAL, and round 3 rendered it as one representative that happened to rebuild a declared term; every other character it admits does not

rows.label: M4_oversized_range
rows.why: a range wider than the bound cannot be enumerated exactly

rows.label: M5_word_category
rows.why: a category class admits members that do not preserve a declared term

rows.label: M6_category_not_space
rows.why: the NEGATED whitespace category. Round 4 tested the exemption with a substring on the category NAME, and the negated name contains the positive one, so the class matching everything EXCEPT whitespace inherited an exemption meant for whitespace. This branch also carries a declared term in another position, so a guard that stops at 'some term is present' reports it clean.
